LESSON OBJECTIVE
Calculate rectangular areas and missing dimensions; apply the area formula to composite regions.
CORE IDEA
Area counts unit squares covering the inside of a rectangle. A rectangle of l columns and w rows contains l times w unit squares.
KEY DEFINITIONS
Length and width are perpendicular sides; area is in squared units such as cm²; perimeter measures boundary length.
CORE RULE
Area A=l×w. To find a missing width, use w=A/l. For a square, A=s².
HOW IT WORKS
Label both perpendicular dimensions, convert to the same units, multiply, and report square units. Reverse with division.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1
A rectangle 7 cm by 4 cm has area 7×4=28 cm². Count 4 rows of 7 unit squares to verify.
WORKED EXAMPLE 2
Area 48 cm² and width 6 cm gives length 48÷6=8 cm. Verify 8×6=48.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3
Perimeter 30 cm and length 9 cm: 2(9+w)=30, w=6 cm, area 9×6=54 cm².
WORKED EXAMPLE 4
Garden 14×9 m has area 126 m²; subtract 2×3 m pond area 6 m² to obtain 120 m².
WORKED EXAMPLE 5
For an 18×10 m lawn with an inside border 2 m wide, interior sides are 14 and 6; area is 84 m².
VERIFIED AREA VISUAL
A grid with 7 columns and 4 rows has exactly 28 cells; the diagram is generated from those integer dimensions.
ADVANCED METHOD
If length is twice width and area is 128, then 2w²=128; w=8 cm, length=16 cm. Only positive dimensions are valid.
COMMON MISTAKES
Do not add sides to find area; do not forget square units; for a border subtract its width at both ends of each dimension.
EXAM STRATEGY
Sketch and label the rectangle, write A=lw, solve the missing dimension, and subtract any excluded regions.
QUICK CHECK
5×8=40 m². Area 63 with length 9 means width 7. Yard 16×9 minus shed 4×3 leaves 132 m².
LESSON RECAP
Area equals length times width. Divide to find an unknown side, and combine rectangular areas to solve composite regions.
